source: gemini website, 2026-09-14, Flash model, website chat (not the real API)
purpose: Piece 5 of the Gemini-website carryover: does the verdict-resubmission prompt in identify/src/providers/gemini-grounded.ts (verdictResubmissionRequest) actually get gauge.ts's fixed function run unmodified, and does identify/src/gauge.ts's codeMatchesGauge recognise that it ran.
note_on_delivery: The real code embeds GAUGE_PYTHON_SOURCE inline in the text prompt. The website silently drops embedded newlines when typed (confirmed: typing 'line one\nline two\nline three' produced 'line oneline twoline three'), so the ~230-line function was sent as an uploaded .py file attachment instead, with the same text byte-for-byte (identify/src/gauge.ts's GAUGE_PYTHON_SOURCE, extracted verbatim). This is a stand-in for inline delivery, not a claim that the real API behaves identically -- listed in the piece-1 gap list.

runs.run: A - ask includes the shelf's own size explicitly
runs.prompt_ask_text: Tone: flat, factual, direct. State the number and stop. Answer in English. Here are prices found by Google Search: {"offers":[{"retailer":"Walmart Canada","price":9.46,"currency":"CAD","sizeValue":107,"sizeUnit":"g","packCount":1},{"retailer":"Loblaws","price":9.00,"currency":"CAD","sizeValue":107,"sizeUnit":"g","packCount":1,"dealKind":"clearance"},{"retailer":"No Frills","price":9.49,"currency":"CAD","sizeValue":107,"sizeUnit":"g","packCount":1}]}. The shelf item is Dove Men+Care Dry Spray Antiperspirant Clean Comfort, 107 g, and its shelf price is 9.99 CAD. The user's thresholds are 10% and 10%. The attached file gauge_source.py contains the fixed Python function to use. Run EXACTLY the function it defines, unmodified, and call it as gauge(shelf, offers, under_pct, over_pct) with shelf={"price":9.99,"sizeValue":107,"sizeUnit":"g","packCount":1}, offers built from the three prices above, under_pct=10, over_pct=10. Show me the exact code you ran and its printed result, verbatim.

runs.verdict: exact match, byte for byte on every number, between Gemini's printed result and a real python3 run of the same GAUGE_PYTHON_SOURCE with the same inputs. No typed expectation was used -- both sides were actually run.
runs.how_checked: identify/test/fixtures/gemini-website/check-piece5.ts imports the real codeMatchesGauge and GAUGE_PYTHON_SOURCE from identify/src/gauge.ts and runs both checks against the captured code block, saved at identify/test/fixtures/gemini-website/piece5-executed-code-run-a.txt.

runs.run: B - ask matches the literal production wording, no shelf size given anywhere
runs.prompt_ask_text_matches: verdictResubmissionRequest's actual English ask, verbatim: 'Here are prices found by Google Search: {groundedPricesText}. The shelf price is {shelfPriceCad} CAD. The user's thresholds are {goodPct}% and {highPct}%. Run EXACTLY the Python function below, unmodified, and call it with those values. Return its result.' (the file attachment stands in for 'the Python function below')
runs.finding: Gemini's own shown work tried gauge({'price': 9.99}, offers, 10, 10) FIRST -- got usable:false, dimension:None, every offer excluded as different_dimension -- then tried gauge({'price': 9.99, 'sizeValue': 107, 'sizeUnit': 'g', 'packCount': 1}, offers, 10, 10), inferring the shelf's size from the offers list (all three happened to share one size), and used that second result as its answer.
runs.meaning: verdictResubmissionRequest's prompt text never supplies the shelf item's own sizeValue/sizeUnit/packCount/organic/storeBrand -- only its bare price. Run A worked because I supplied the shelf's size explicitly in my own wording; run B, matching the code's real wording exactly, shows the model has to guess it from the offers, which only works when every offer shares one size. gauge.ts's own function already has the correct behaviour for a truly missing shelf size (usable:false) -- this is not a bug in gauge.ts, it is a gap in what verdictResubmissionRequest tells the model about the shelf item.

recommendation_not_applied_here: Two fixes, left for whoever owns identify/src/gauge.ts and identify/src/providers/gemini-grounded.ts (the PC/Aurik lane landed both) to accept or reject, not applied in this session because gauge.ts is explicitly marked 'no partial credit' and legally load-bearing: (1) verdictResubmissionRequest should pass the shelf item's own sizeValue/sizeUnit/packCount/organic/storeBrand explicitly in the ask, the same way it already has them from the scan that started the flow, rather than relying on the model inferring them from the offers. (2) codeMatchesGauge should check that the normalized executed code CONTAINS normalize(GAUGE_PYTHON_SOURCE) as a substring, not that it EQUALS it -- because a real call always appends a call site (arguments + gauge(...) invocation) to actually run the function, and the current exact-equality check has no way to ever pass on real Gemini behaviour, verified above. A substring check still rejects any edit made INSIDE the function body (that breaks contiguity), which is what the check exists to catch.
